initial_requirements: A university needs a Unified University Inventory System that combines the inventory databases of three faculties and makes the integrated inventory available through a secure web interface. University, faculty, and department staff need to manage assets such as rooms, software licences, and equipment, while other users should be able to request assets or reserve spaces for approval by the appropriate administrative level.

slots.key: Primary consolidation goal
slots.value: Create one secure source of truth for all inventory across the university so staff can manage and access assets consistently instead of working in separate faculty systems.

slots.key: Change proposal, approval, and notification workflow for shared definitions
slots.value: Change proposals should be allowed from university-level admins and faculty admins. Approval should sit with the university inventory owner or a central governance group to maintain one source of truth across all three faculties. Once approved, changes should be announced through the system itself and by email to affected departments so nobody uses outdated definitions. The affected departments should be determined by which faculty, department, or asset category the change actually touches, so only people who rely on that definition get the notice. Urgent policy or approval changes that could cause mistakes right away should be notified immediately; routine or planned changes can be scheduled for the next business day or a maintenance window to avoid unnecessary interruption. There should be a standard set of request statuses across all faculties, and only the central inventory team should be able to change that definition. Faculties must not invent their own meanings for the same status; any local variation should be mapped back to the standard status set. The default should be to notify only the directly affected departments, faculties, or asset categories. Broader notice is needed only for university-wide policy impact, a legal requirement, or a technical dependency that could affect other users or systems. In those cases, timing may also need to change if waiting would create compliance or operational risk.
